title: Chloride–bicarbonate interaction does not improve serum potassium prediction across two NHANES cycles
abstract: A prespecified chloride-by-bicarbonate interaction failed to improve serum potassium prediction over additive nonlinear standard laboratory measures: source PSU-grouped cross-validation MSE reduction −0.00011626; frozen transfer from 5,230 NHANES 2007–08 adults to 5,629 adults in 2009–10 gave reduction −0.00002449 (mmol/L)², with two-sample refit PSU-bootstrap 95% interval [−0.00026579, 0.00010444]. This is a negative incremental-prediction result in independent cycles within one survey program, not external-program validation or evidence against acid–base physiology.
